papers_read.title_as_printed: A Graph Gaussian Embedding Method for Predicting Alzheimer's Disease Progression with MEG Brain Networks (Xu et al., IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2021;68(5):1579-1588, author manuscript)

STCWTNet: Spatio-temporal channel-wise transformer network for interpretable cross-subject mild cognitive impairment detection using EEG signals (Liu et al., Biomedical Signal Processing and Control 118 (2026) 109564)

what_each_reports.P-173: Resting-state alpha-band MEG functional networks (68 Desikan-Killiany ROIs) from 53 NC and 76 MCI-due-to-AD patients (Hospital Universitario San Carlos, Madrid), MCI followed ~3 years into sMCI (n=48) and pMCI (n=28). MG2G graph embeddings fed to 10 classifiers, 5-fold CV, mean accuracy across classifiers: 61% (3-class), 79% NC/sMCI, 78% sMCI/pMCI, 82% NC/pMCI. AUCs are shown only in supplementary figures; the main text states no AUC value, so the record's 'AUC 0.81' cannot be checked against this extract.
what_each_reports.P-129: Resting eyes-closed 19-channel EEG from the public Isfahan dataset (32 MCI, 29 HC), STCWTNet transformer, subject-wise 6x5 nested CV repeated 20 times, MCI vs HC detection: accuracy 90.97% ± 0.60, specificity 94.76% ± 0.78, sensitivity 86.87% ± 1.14, AUC 0.950 ± 0.006. It contains no conversion (pMCI vs sMCI) analysis.

quantity_a: Cross-validated discrimination (mean accuracy across classifiers; AUC only in supplement) of MEG network embeddings for sMCI vs pMCI (~3-year conversion to AD) and related NC/sMCI/pMCI contrasts, Madrid MEG cohort
quantity_b: Subject-wise nested-CV accuracy/specificity/AUC for current MCI vs healthy control detection from resting EEG, Isfahan public dataset
incompatible_if_same: No comparison arises: the record's 'Acc 94.76' is P-129's specificity (its accuracy is 90.97%), and it is an MCI-vs-HC detection figure, not a conversion figure; it is also set against an AUC. A specificity and an AUC for different contrasts cannot disagree.

gates.task: mismatch: P-173's contested figure is conversion prediction (sMCI vs pMCI, T2); P-129 is MCI vs HC detection (T1). The record's 'Acc 94.76 on T2' and task_equal='Yes' are wrong; no waiver on record
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Madrid San Carlos MEG cohort vs the Isfahan (Sina and Nour hospitals) public EEG dataset; the record's dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong
gates.modality_family: match at family level: electrophysiology (MEG vs EEG, both resting-state)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: different endpoint (3-year conversion vs current MCI status) and different metric types (AUC vs a specificity mislabelled as accuracy)
performance_validity: flag does not apply to the contested figures: P-129's cross-subject nested-CV AUC is 0.950 (<0.97); its intra-subject 10-fold results on 27/34-subject subsets (AUC 0.979/0.987) are not the figure the record uses
independence: Independent: different groups, countries, cohorts and recording modalities; no shared authors.
grounds: The record misreads P-129: 94.76% is its specificity, not its accuracy (90.97%).
The record also misreads P-129's task: it detects current MCI vs healthy controls and has no conversion analysis, so 'on T2' is wrong.
A detection specificity set against a conversion AUC describes no disagreement; in addition the task and dataset-family gates fail with no waiver on record.
P-173's main text reports only accuracies (78% sMCI/pMCI) and places AUCs in the supplement, so the record's 'AUC 0.81' is not verifiable from the extract.

evidence_quotes.quote: the stable MCI group (sMCI, n = 48) comprising those patients that still fulfilled the diagnosis criteria of MCI at the end of follow-up, and the progressive MCI group (pMCI, n = 28) comprising those patients that met the criteria for probable AD
MG2G achieved high performance with 61% for NC/sMCI/pMCI classification, 79% for NC/sMCI classification, 78% for sMCI/pMCI classification, and 82% for NC/pMCI classification.
Receiver operating characteristic area-under-the-curve (AUC) plots are shown in Suppl. Figs. 1 and 2.
STCWTNet achieves 90.97% accuracy, 94.76% specificity, 86.87% sensitivity, and 0.950 AUC, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods.
The dataset comprised 32 subjects diagnosed with MCI and 29 healthy controls, all aged over 55 years with at least an elementary education.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-129: Acc 94.76 on T2' is wrong twice: 94.76% is specificity (accuracy is 90.97%), and the task is MCI vs HC detection (T1), not conversion.
task_equal='Yes' and dataset_equal='Yes' are wrong (conversion vs detection; Madrid MEG vs Isfahan EEG).
claim_a 'P-173: AUC 0.81' is not stated in the main text of the P-173 extract, which reports accuracies only and puts AUCs in supplementary figures.
P-129 registry Best_Metric 'Acc 94.76' repeats the specificity-as-accuracy error; its Method_Architecture field holds abstract spillover text.
The 'bridging evidence' list (e.g. P-369, whose block is recorded elsewhere as fabricated) names no condition separating the two results.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers: P-129 has no conversion result. A genuine candidate would need another MEG/EEG study predicting sMCI vs pMCI over a comparable horizon with an AUC whose interval excludes P-173's.
